'''Bjorn Mikhail Poonen''' (born July 27, 1968, in [[Boston]], Massachusetts) is a mathematician, four-time [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition|Putnam Competition]] winner, and a Distinguished Professor in Science in the Department of Mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="MIT Mathematics m059">{{cite web | title=Profile | website=MIT Mathematics | url=https://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.html?pid=213 | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref>  
His research is primarily in [[arithmetic geometry]], but he has occasionally published in other subjects such as [[probability]]<ref>Amir Dembo, Qi-Man Shao, Bjorn Poonen, and Ofer Zeitouni, "Random polynomials with few or no real zeros", ''[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]'' '''15''' (2002), 857–892.</ref> and [[computer science]].<ref name="Poonen 1993 pp. 101–124">{{cite journal | last=Poonen | first=Bjorn | title=The Worst Case in Shellsort and Related Algorithms | journal=Journal of Algorithms | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=15 | issue=1 | year=1993 | issn=0196-6774 | doi=10.1006/jagm.1993.1032 | pages=101–124| citeseerx=10.1.1.138.295 }}</ref>
He has edited two books.<ref name="Kedlaya Poonen Vakil 2011 p. ">{{cite book | last1=Kedlaya | first1=Kiran S. | last2=Poonen | first2=Bjorn | last3=Vakil | first3=Ravi | title=The William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition 1985–2000 | publisher=Mathematical Association of America | date=March 24, 2011 | isbn=978-0-88385-827-1 | page=}}</ref><ref name="Birkhäuser Boston 2004 p. ">{{cite book | title=Progress in Mathematics | chapter=Arithmetic of Higher-Dimensional Algebraic Varieties | publisher=Birkhäuser Boston | publication-place=Boston, MA | year=2004 | volume=226 | isbn=978-1-4612-6471-2 | issn=0743-1643 | doi=10.1007/978-0-8176-8170-8 | page=}}</ref>
  
He is the founding managing editor of the journal ''[[Algebra & Number Theory]]'',<ref name="MSP 2005 b590">{{cite web | title=Algebra & Number Theory | website=MSP | date=May 2, 2005 | url=https://msp.org/ant/about/journal/editorial.html | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref> and serves also on the editorial boards of ''[[Involve: A Journal of Mathematics]]''<ref name="msp.org 2007 x371">{{cite web | title=Involve | website=msp.org | date=May 2, 2007 | url=https://msp.org/involve/about/journal/editorial.html | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref> and the ''[[A K Peters]] Research Notes in Mathematics'' book series.<ref name="cv">[http://www-math.mit.edu/~poonen/papers/cv.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved January 28, 2015.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Poonen was born on July 27, 1968 in Boston to an Indian father and Norwegian-American mother.<ref name="p927">{{cite web | title=Math Prof Receives Packard Fellowship | publisher=Office of Public Affairs, UC Berkeley | date=1998-11-18 | url=https://newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/berkeleyan/1998/1118/mathprof.html }}</ref> He attended the [[Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics]] while a student at [[Winchester High School (Massachusetts)|Winchester High School]] in [[Winchester, Massachusetts]], where he graduated in 1985.<ref name="e976">{{cite journal | last=Page | first=Warren | title=An Interview with the 1985 USA Team to the International Mathematical Olympiad | journal=The College Mathematics Journal | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=16 | issue=5 | year=1985 | issn=0746-8342 | doi=10.1080/07468342.1985.11972907 | pages=336–360}}</ref> In 1989, Poonen graduated from [[Harvard University]] with an [[A.B.]] in Mathematics and Physics, summa cum laude. He then studied under [[Kenneth Alan Ribet]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], completing a PhD there in 1994.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|32425}}</ref>

==Academic positions==
Poonen held postdoctoral positions at [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] and [[Princeton University]] and served on the faculty of the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1997 to 2008, before moving to [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]].<ref name="cv"/>
He has also held visiting positions at the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] (1998 and 2005), the [[Paris-Sud 11 University|Université Paris-Sud]] (2001), Harvard  (2007), and MIT (2007).<ref name="cv"/>

==Major honors and awards==
* [[Joseph L. Doob Prize]], 2023<ref name="American Mathematical Society 2018 t179">{{cite web | title=Joseph L. Doob Prize | website=American Mathematical Society | date=November 26, 2018 | url=http://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=21 | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]], 2012.<ref name="American Mathematical Society 2018 u222">{{cite web | title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society | website=American Mathematical Society | date=November 26, 2018 | url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi | access-date=October 14, 2023}}</ref>
* [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]: elected in 2012<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.amacad.org/members.aspx|title=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|website=www.amacad.org|access-date=October 23, 2016}}</ref>
* [[Chauvenet Prize]]: the 2011 winner, for his article "Undecidability in number theory"<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/22/?pa=content&sa=viewDocument&nodeId=1604|title=Chauvenet Prizes {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=mathdl.maa.org|access-date=October 23, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Undecidability">{{citation|last=Poonen|first=Bjorn|title=Undecidability in Number Theory|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=March 2008|pages=344–350|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200803/tx080300344p.pdf}}</ref>
* [[Miller Institute|Miller]] Research Professorship – University of California Berkeley.
* [[David and Lucile Packard Foundation|David and Lucile Packard Fellowship]]<ref>[http://www.cs.virginia.edu/packard/directory/field/mathematics.html Packard fellows in mathematics] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080415174638/http://www.cs.virginia.edu/packard/directory/field/mathematics.html |date=April 15, 2008 }}</ref>
* [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellowship]]<ref>''[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society|Notices Amer. Math. Soc.]]'' '''45''', no. 6, (June–July 1998), p. 723.</ref>
* [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]]: winner in 1985, 1986, 1987, and 1988 (the only other four-time winners since 1938 are [[Don Coppersmith]], [[Arthur Rubin]], [[Ravi D. Vakil]], [[Gabriel Carroll]], [[Reid W. Barton]], [[Daniel Kane (mathematician)|Daniel Kane]] and [[Brian R. Lawrence]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/awards/putnam.html|title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|access-date=October 23, 2016|archive-date=February 29, 2000|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000229230334/http://www.maa.org/awards/putnam.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]: silver medalist in 1985.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=9627|title=International Mathematical Olympiad|website=www.imo-official.org|access-date=October 23, 2016}}</ref>
* [[American Mathematics Competitions|American High School Mathematics Examination]]: only participant (out of 380,000) to receive a perfect score in 1985.<ref>[https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20081031153754/http://www.unl.edu/amc/d-publication/d1-pubarchive/2004-5pub/2005-HSsummary.pdf American High School Mathematics Examination results], page 31</ref>

==Trivia==

Kenneth | last2=Poonen | first2=Bjorn | last3=Poonen | first3=George | title=How to Spread Rumors Fast | journal=Mathematics Magazine | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=70 | issue=1 | year=1997 | issn=0025-570X | doi=10.1080/0025570x.1997.11996496 | pages=40–42}}</ref>
